subject: Adult-use cannabis requirements carried by Policies and Procedures rather than adopted regulations
instrument_type: agency policy and procedure (not a chapter 54 regulation)
authority: RERACA provisions authorizing the Commissioner to establish policies and procedures pending regulations
status: in effect as the agency’s stated position
progress_status: never converted into adopted regulations for the adult-use market
outcome: The adult-use testing and operating requirements sit in a policy document, not in the Regulations of Connecticut State Agencies.
note: This is why the October 2026 question matters: a policy is not a regulation, and the difference decides what survives a challenge.

subject: medical — Microbial limit / method
date: 2012 (medical regulations as first adopted; text shown in brackets in PR2017-029)
progress_status: baseline
outcome: "For purposes of the microbiological test, a marijuana sample shall be deemed to have passed if it satisfies the standards set forth in Section 1111 of the United States Pharmacopeia"
note: DCP Chapter 54 rulemaking (2012) | USP <1111> numbers not reproduced here (paywalled; TIER 3 reproductions only).

subject: medical — Failure disposition / retest
progress_status: baseline; no retest or remediation pathway in the regulation text at any date
outcome: "If a sample of marijuana does not pass the microbiological, mycotoxin, heavy metal or pesticide chemical residue test ... the producer shall dispose of the entire batch from which the sample was taken"
note: DCP | CGS 21a-408w (from 2024-07-01) permits repeat testing/remediation; which governs medical after 2026-10-01 is L-0170.

subject: medical — Sampling; reporting of failures to DCP
progress_status: baseline
outcome: "(b) A producer shall make available each such batch at the production facility for a laboratory employee to select a random sample." ... "(g) The laboratory shall file with the department an electronic copy of each laboratory test result for any batch that does not pass ... at the same time that it transmits those results to the producer."
note: DCP | AltaSci COAs 2017-2023 print "Sample(s) tested were collected at the Customer's production facility from lot(s) as designated by the Customer" (5,323 of 5,507 AltaSci PDFs). Failure filings under (g) are not public: queued request L37-OR-01.

subject: medical — Heavy metals
progress_status: baseline (unchanged 2018, 2022)
outcome: "a marijuana sample shall be deemed to have passed if it meets the following standards: Metal Natural Health Products Acceptable limits uG/KG BW/Day Arsenic <0.14 Cadmium <0.09 Lead <0.29 Mercury <0.29"
note: DCP | Limits are daily-intake figures (per kg body weight per day), not concentrations; a lab must assume an intake to apply them. AltaSci printed As <4.206, Cd <2.704, Hg/Pb <8.712 ug/g = exactly 30.04 x the regulation figures (STRONG INFERENCE: 60 kg body weight / ~2 g per day); its 2022-23 template printed the raw figures as "< 0.14 ug/Kg" etc. No DCP instruction on the conversion was found.

subject: medical — Mycotoxins; pesticides
progress_status: mycotoxin method (LC-MS or ELISA) added 2022
outcome: "less than 20 micrograms per kilogram of each of ... aflatoxin B1, aflatoxin B2, aflatoxin G1, aflatoxin G2, and ochratoxin A" (2022 wording); pesticides: "the most stringent acceptable standard for a pesticide chemical residue in any food item as set forth in ... 40 CFR 180"
note: DCP |

subject: medical — Microbial limit
progress_status: raw product moved from USP <1111> to USP <2023>
outcome: "a marijuana sample shall be deemed to have passed if it satisfies the standards set forth in Section 2023 of the United States Pharmacopeia for all raw products and Section 1111 of the United States Pharmacopeia for all dosage forms other than rawproduct"
note: DCP Chapter 54 rulemaking PR2017-029 | USP <2023> TYMC 10^3 for dried botanicals is from reproductions (TIER 3); DCP (2022-03-16) called 10^3 a misstatement.

subject: medical — AltaSci yeast/mould criterion
instrument_type: Reported private email approval (no published instrument)
authority: Reported private email approval (no published instrument)
progress_status: lab-specific criterion outside any published instrument
outcome: NOT HELD. Reported: DCP approved by email in August 2020 AltaSci's request to raise its yeast/mould passing level from 10,000 to 1,000,000 CFU/g, paired with Aspergillus testing.
note: AltaSci request; DCP Drug Control approval (reported) | Certificates: 10^6 TYMC printed 2020-08-31..2020-12-09 (no Aspergillus test printed on any of 83 window-A certificates) and 2021-07-20..2022-01-21 (all 114 print it). Emails queued L5 OR-01.

If the sample yields satisfactory results ..., an employee from a different laboratory shall select a
note: DCP | From 2023-Q3 through 2024-Q3 Northeast Laboratories issued 100% of registry-linked certificates (T1); a "different laboratory" did not operate in the registry record (AltaSci last registration 2023-Q2; ACTL.0000005 issued 2024-09-13 per L20). subject: adult use — Microbial limit
outcome: Numeric standard 10^5 TAMC / 10^5 TYMC with named non-detects (text held: runs/S4-ALTASCI-20260921 docs; LIMITS_IN_FORCE.csv)
note: DCP | Magnitude caveat C-217/C-373: write as yeast-and-mould figure; aerobic count unchanged.

subject: medical — Microbial limit; method; pathogens; Aspergillus
progress_status: USP <2023> -> 10^5; qPCR; named pathogen and Aspergillus non-detects; 180-day qPCR grace
outcome: "tested using a molecular method that is certified for identifying microbiological DNA and approved by the Association of Official Analytical Collaboration (AOAC) International and includes quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) ... deemed satisfactory if (A) E. coli, shiga toxin producing E. coli, L. monocytogenes, and salmonella spp. are not detected, (B) the total aerobic microbial count and total combined yeast and mold count are each equal to or less than 105 cfu/g or ml, and (C) the pathogenic Aspergillus species A. fumigatus, A. flavus, A. niger, and A. terreus are not detected."
note: DCP Chapter 54 (notice 2021-12-29; AG 2022-03-29; LRRC 2022-05-24) | Culture (CFU) and qPCR results are not interchangeable (A-112).
